title: Positive pressure versus BP in a preload-dependent patient
subtitle: Hemodynamic consequences of positive intrathoracic pressure in severe preload dependency
ruleBasedNote: Hemodynamic response to mean alveolar pressure (ppvResponse = clean-kill) is a rule-based circulation model, not a mechanistic cardiovascular simulation.

patient.summary: A 68-year-old mechanically ventilated patient with distributive shock and intravascular volume depletion receiving volume-controlled ventilation.

prediction.question: When PEEP is elevated from 5 to 16 cmH2O in this preload-dependent patient, how do mean airway pressure (Pmean), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and heart rate respond?

whatToLookAtHint: Watch the mean airway pressure on the ventilator alongside systolic blood pressure and heart rate on the bedside monitor.

reflection.question: Why does escalating PEEP from 5 to 16 cmH2O precipitate profound hypotension and tachycardia in this patient?

options.text: Elevated mean alveolar and intrathoracic pressure increases right atrial pressure, reducing the pressure gradient for systemic venous return (MSFP - RAP) and drastically lowering right ventricular stroke volume.
High airway pressure triggers direct cholinergic vagal discharge that dilates systemic arterioles.
Excess positive pressure directly compresses the ascending aorta and precipitates acute myocardial ischemia.
PEEP relaxes abdominal vascular tone by mechanical vibration of the celiac plexus.

reflection.explanation: In hypovolemic and preload-dependent circulations (phenotype 'clean-kill'), cardiac filling is precarious. Venous return is driven by the pressure gradient between mean systemic filling pressure (MSFP) and right atrial pressure (RAP). Increasing PEEP from 5 to 16 cmH2O raises mean airway pressure (from ~7 to ~18 cmH2O). Transmission of this positive pressure into the pericardial space increases RAP, attenuating venous return, stroke volume, and cardiac output. Consequently, systolic blood pressure plummets (from ~110 to ~75 mmHg) while reflex baroreceptor activation elevates heart rate.

evidence.claim: Positive intrathoracic pressure increases right atrial pressure and impedes venous return, which significantly reduces cardiac output in preload-dependent patients.
evidence.source: Pinsky MR. Cardiopulmonary interactions: the basics. Curr Opin Crit Care 2007; 13(1):3-10.

evidence.claim: Increasing positive end-expiratory pressure in volume-depleted states produces significant left ventricular stroke volume reduction via decreased right ventricular filling.
evidence.source: Jardin F, Farcot JC, Boisnante L, et al. Influence of positive end-expiratory pressure on left ventricular performance. N Engl J Med 1981; 304(7):387-392.
